# Fully charged favourable relaxation for a k-call shared centre window

**Scoped planning result for the `centre-path-sharing` card (construction reading of its method 1). No shared centre is constructed or admitted, no supplier admission, no new kappa; the selected record is unchanged.**

Agent: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no model named; no independent human review claimed).

Package: `research/centre-shared-kcall-charged-seed615415` (branch `research/agent-85-184695337c-615415`, base `d8e0f83f00191df62174b641e9fff055c357f641`; canonical main unchanged at the pre-submission fetch). Task card: `centre-path-sharing`, scope status `unchanged`, drawn by `scripts/choose_research_task.py` (seed `615415b58548f9dea7ddac4165b1e2e2`, cards `centre-path-sharing`, `joint-query-controller`, `coverage-law-change`). No live claim on this object existed in discussions 1166 or 1317 at draw time; a claim was posted before computation at https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18983433

## What this adds

The card's construction method asks for a fully charged favourable relaxation for sharing one centre path across k calls, including restoration, hosting and precision. Prior packages priced pieces: `research/centre-sharing-overhead-budget` gives tolerable overhead budgets and explicitly leaves hosting, precision and the overhead form unpriced; `research/centre-shared-return-guard` prices the pinned two-panel macro bill and its precision boundary but never converts to rank mass or a ceiling; the observation-floor packages supply no restoration, hosting or precision bill at all. This package does the conversion for the one sharing pattern with a pinned contract (the shared-sink return window of [PR 1708](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1708) / [PR 1748](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1748), credit 1337isnot1337 / Cinna Davis and ToikY), generalised to k panels, charges all three named costs explicitly, and reports `ceiling.ceiling(centre=...)` for the changed profiles.

## Conversion contract

The pinned guard's literal backward centre-phase bill is 16 rank-8 returns, 368 ADDs, 32 CLEARs per two literal phases and 8, 360, 16 for the two-call fused window; the k = 1 and k = 2 formulas reproduce all six numbers exactly. One fused k-call window gathers k panels before one ascent per centre and writes the shared sink once.

| Item | Charge in rank-mass units |
| --- | --- |
| One rank-8 COPY/ERASE total | one rank-8 child = 8 units (ascent and erase inside) |
| One ADD | one rank-1 child |
| One scratch CLEAR | one rank-1 child (restoration of the private temporary) |
| Hosting shared rows across the window | 0, under the idle-axis-hosting lemma and its window constraints |
| Precision for k summed panels | `ceil(log2 k)` magnitude bits, one rank-1 unit per shared total per bit per window |

Per call, a literal phase pays 8 rank-8 + 184 ADD + 8 scratch CLEAR; a fused k-call window pays `8/k` rank-8, `176 + 8/k` ADD and `8/k` scratch CLEAR. The consumer readout is unchanged: the fused window writes the same endpoint rows as the separate phases, so readout is neither saved nor added.

## Results: changed centre charge, copy profile, charged ceiling

Exact brackets at grid `1e-12`; ratios against the baseline ceiling `0.001690054109...`; kappa via the retained planning transfer `a/(1+a)`.

| k | centre per call | copy children rank-8 per call | restoration per call | hosting | precision rank-1 per call | gross ceiling | fully charged ceiling | kappa cap | ratio |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 64 | 8 | 8 | 0 | 0 | 0.001690054110 | 0.001690054110 | 0.001687202646 | 1.000 |
| 2 | 32 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 4 | 0.003217794406 | 0.003215381840 | 0.003205076296 | 1.903 |
| 4 | 16 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 4 | 0.003984054054 | 0.003981062728 | 0.003965276713 | 2.356 |
| 8 | 8 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 3 | 0.004367783311 | 0.004365321517 | 0.004346348309 | 2.583 |
| 16 | 4 | 1/2 | 1/2 | 0 | 2 | 0.004559798056 | 0.004558083777 | 0.004537401919 | 2.697 |

The k = 1 row reproduces the selected word and the published baseline ceiling. Charging restoration, hosting and precision moves the k = 2 ceiling by 0.075 per cent. Rows k at or above 4 use the derived k-panel generalisation, not a pinned construction.

## Break-even overhead at k = 2 (extra rank-1 children per call)

| Treatment | keep full bit-limited gain | at c_bit | any gain over selected |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| overhead displaces idle mass (coverage identity kept) | 1650, identity-feasible maximum | 1650, identity-feasible maximum | 1650, identity-feasible maximum |
| overhead adds pure moment (predecessor treatment) | 31 | 31 | 32 |

Both are sharp (H passes the exact moment test and H+1 fails) except where the coverage identity caps them. Under the ceiling model's accounting the window absorbs the entire idle remainder of 1650 rank-1 units per call and still clears the complex-unbinding point `T2 = 1733427039589844234749/(10^24 - 1)`. Under the additive treatment of `centre-sharing-overhead-budget`, 31 rank-1 children per call fit before the full bit-limited gain is lost; their sharp budgets are `4415/144 = 30.66` and `4591/144 = 31.88` per call, and this verifier recomputes 30.98 and 32.19 (ratios 1.010, 1.010; the difference is ideal-packing versus actual-histogram moment).

The card's screen passes on its own metric (ideal shared-by-two ratio 1.90 against the 1.10 stop threshold, levers.py). The whole-bound gain is a different quantity: the bit supplier binds at `c_bit = 0.001733427039589844234749`, capping any such mechanism at `kappa = 865213734911801/5*10^17 = 0.001730427469823602` (+3.4536 per cent over the selected record, per `centre-sharing-overhead-budget`). For this pattern the named costs are not the blocker; eligibility and demand coupling are.

## Controls (enforced, not advisory)

- k = 1 and k = 2 conversion formulas reproduce the pinned separate bill (16/368/32) and fused bill (8/360/16) exactly, and the precision bit count matches the pinned guard.
- k = 1 profile equals the selected word and reproduces the published baseline ceiling to the grid.
- One extra rank-1 child lowers the k = 2 charged ceiling; a doubled precision charge lowers it again.
- Every break-even is sharp, or explicitly capped by identity feasibility.
- Additive identity-profile budgets stay within a factor of two of `centre-sharing-overhead-budget` (measured 1.010 and 1.010).

## Scope and limits

- One sharing pattern only: a fused window whose k calls share sink rows, return operator and chart. Eligibility is granted, not shown. `centre-shared-return-guard` supplies neither a full pair of fused local calls nor an eligible owner pair; `research/p112-batch-centre-floor` proves independent root-code demands cannot share at all (copied-pairing-rank bill `64k`), so the pattern needs genuinely coupled demands.
- The macro-to-rank-mass conversion is stated, not inherited (each scalar total pays one child at its pairing rank); a different conversion changes the rows.
- Hosting is charged zero mass on the idle-axis-hosting lemma with its window constraints named; a window crossed by an observation or checkpoint cannot host, and then the per-use copy and erase return with no saving.
- Precision is charged at the sufficient bit count for positive envelopes only. The pinned guard does not establish rounding-error, native guard, tape or global admission, and fused primitives at width `mu+1` price at the invoice level, outside this mass model.
- Fractional child counts are allowed, as in the incumbent ceiling model. No kappa, supplier or eligible-pair claim.

## Reproduce

Standard library only, Python 3.12, from the repository root:

```text
python3 -I -B research/centre-shared-kcall-charged-seed615415/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/centre-shared-kcall-charged-seed615415 --check-only
python3 scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/centre-shared-kcall-charged-seed615415
```

Recorded outputs: `PASS_CENTRE_SHARED_KCALL_CHARGED k2_charged_ceiling 0.003215381840 k2_ratio 1.902532 H_bit_displace 1650 H_bit_additive 31 H_any_additive 32 no_new_kappa`, `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`, `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`, and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/centre-shared-kcall-charged-seed615415 outcome=completed` from the registered 3.12 replay.

## Open next questions

1. Is any selected call pair eligible for a fused shared-sink window (shared post-A rows, identical return operator and chart, uninterrupted window)? First step: extract the backward centre-phase invocations of two sink-sharing calls from the selected replay schedule. Blocked by: owner map and schedule are not in the package; the guard leaves eligibility open.
2. Which selected call pairs have coupled rather than independent demands? First step: classify the 144 selected calls by shared sink rows and return operator. Blocked by: no machine-readable demand-coupling table exists.
3. Does the fused primitive bill at width `mu+1` fit the selected invoice guard? First step: instantiate the pinned fused bill under the selected invoice formulas. Blocked by: actual tariffs and precision headroom are uninstantiated.

## Credit and attribution

Sharing constructions: [PR 1708](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1708) "Finite centre-phase fanout across two shared-source panels" by 1337isnot1337 (Cinna Davis) and [PR 1748](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1748) "Certify shared reverse centre phase with a charged precision guard" by ToikY (both authors verified against current GitHub metadata at writing time). The pinned two-panel contract, its exact bill and its one-magnitude-bit precision guard are ToikY's `research/centre-shared-return-guard`, used unchanged as a pinned input. The packing-ceiling model, lever table and coverage identity are Douglas Colkitt's `research/complex-local-word-ceiling` and [PR 1012](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1012) "Research note: restoration deferral is mass-neutral in the hosted T37 recurrence (no new kappa)" by thakrarsagar. Additive overhead budgets and the bit endpoint are `research/centre-sharing-overhead-budget` (prepared for rtyu193-rgb with Claude Code assistance). The hosting lemma is `research/idle-axis-hosting`. The `64k` floor for independent demands is `research/p112-batch-centre-floor`, crediting Mihir Srivastava's PR 845, Adam Gall's PR 1098 and woklerx's PR 1180.
